correctness.rationale: The source's exact homogeneous shadow theorem applies because every \(A_i\) contains zero. At degree \(m-1\), the complete monomial list is \(M_i=\prod_{j\ne i}x_j\). Each shadow is exactly the disjoint union of the all-positive exponent core of size \(P\) and one zero slice of size \(P/(n_i-1)\). Hence the shadow of any \(r\)-subset has exact size \(P+\sum P_i\), and sorting the \(n_i\) gives the stated minimum. The projective formula follows from the source's all-r affine/projective scaling relation. A direct finite-field subcode census independently matches the theorem.

value.rationale: The weight hierarchy is the central invariant studied by the source and has wiretap-channel meaning. The edge degree \(d=m-1\) is a natural high-degree family of dimension \(m\), yet the source's broad explicit formula supplies only its first two weights. The accepted theorem closes that entire hierarchy in one expression and gives an equally complete projective family. This is a structural formula across arbitrary Cartesian sizes, not a finite or routine table extension.
